name: devries2021_mink
citation: de Vries L, Koopmans M, Morton A, van Baal P (2021) The economics of improving global infectious disease surveillance. BMJ Global Health 6(9):e006597
licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); only the numbers of Box 2 are transcribed, as facts, with their source
retrieved: 2026-11-25, full text XML from Europe PMC (PMC8413876); Box 2 and its footnotes read in full
decision: Whether to close a mink farm that may be infected with SARS-CoV-2, for each of about 125 farms in the Netherlands, and what information on which farms are infected would be worth
unit: millions of euros (the paper's figures: the cost of closing a farm is from earlier research; the cost of an infected farm left open and the share of farms infected are, in the authors' words, 'hypothetical and generated solely to illustrate the principle')

box2.provenance: Box 2, 'Value of information and the closure of mink farms'
box2.implied: A farm that is open and not infected costs nothing, and closing costs the same whether or not the farm is infected; the box does not print these two cells but uses them (10% x -10 = -1; 'only 10% of the farms will be closed with an expected loss of 50 million').
